question: persister
prompt:
Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Retrospective profiling of future survivors via sibling-cell splitting
ideas.description: Barcode a clonal population, split it into twin dishes, treat one with drug, and use the barcodes of the survivors to go back and sequence or image their untreated siblings. This directly measures the pre-treatment state of cells destined to survive, rather than inferring it from survivors after the drug has already reshaped them.

ideas.title: Fluctuation analysis to measure the memory timescale of the primed state
ideas.description: Expand single cells into many sibling subclones, treat each, and compare the variance in survivor number against a Poisson expectation, Luria-Delbruck style. Repeating this with different expansion times converts the variance into an estimate of how many generations the survival-conferring state is inherited, separating a heritable epigenetic state from a purely instantaneous stochastic one.

ideas.title: Prospective sorting to test sufficiency, not just correlation
ideas.description: Use a live marker of the candidate primed state (surface protein stain or a knock-in reporter) to sort the rare high cells before any drug exposure, then measure their survival frequency against sorted-low and unsorted cells. Enrichment that falls far short of the marker's purity would reveal the state is necessary but not sufficient, pointing to a second required factor.

ideas.title: Single-cell apoptotic priming as an alternative explanation to signaling state
ideas.description: Apply BH3 profiling or a single-cell cytochrome c release assay before treatment to measure how close each cell sits to the apoptotic threshold. This tests the distinct hypothesis that survivors are not signaling outliers but simply cells with more buffered mitochondria, an explanation that transcriptomics alone would miss.

ideas.title: Cross-drug barcode overlap to ask whether priming is drug-specific
ideas.description: Split one barcoded population across several mechanistically distinct drugs and compare which barcodes appear among the survivors of each. Strong overlap would imply a general tolerant state such as slow cycling, while near-disjoint survivor sets would argue for many independent, pathway-specific primed states, a result that changes which combination therapies make sense.

candidates: Lineage barcoding with sister-cell splitting to retrospectively profile the pre-treatment transcriptome of cells that later survive
Luria-Delbruck style fluctuation analysis across sibling subclones to separate heritable priming from stochastic drug-induced response
Barcode-based measurement of state memory half-life: re-split resistant colonies, re-treat, and ask how long survival propensity persists
Live imaging with ERK/AKT biosensors through treatment to link signaling dynamics before drug to eventual survival
Single-molecule RNA FISH for candidate resistance markers to count rare primed cells and quantify their co-expression structure
Single-cell multiome (RNA + ATAC) on sorted primed cells to find accessibility changes that precede expression changes
Targeted sorting of rare marker-high cells before treatment, then direct survival assay to test sufficiency of the primed state
Time-resolved scRNA-seq across the drug-tolerant bottleneck to distinguish selection of pre-existing cells from induced reprogramming
Pooled CRISPR screen performed specifically in the primed subpopulation versus the bulk to find modifiers of priming rather than of growth
Metabolic single-cell imaging (NAD(P)H lifetime, lipid peroxidation sensors) to test whether survivors are a metabolic rather than transcriptional outlier
Cell-cycle and quiescence reporters to test whether survival is simply explained by being in a slow or arrested state at dosing
Drug uptake and efflux measured per cell with fluorescent drug analogs to test the boring but underexcluded pharmacokinetic explanation
Measuring cell-intrinsic variability in target occupancy via phospho-target immunofluorescence at single-cell resolution
Spatial analysis of whether survivors cluster, implicating local microenvironment or paracrine signaling rather than cell-autonomous state
Conditioned-media and co-culture swaps to test whether survivors create a protective niche for neighbors
Mitochondrial apoptotic priming (BH3 profiling) at single-cell resolution to test whether survival is set by death-threshold rather than signaling
Protein-level single-cell measurement (CyTOF or 4i) to check whether transcriptional priming actually propagates to protein
Clonal barcode overlap across independent drugs to test whether the same cells are primed for multiple therapies or drug-specific priming exists
Micro-raft or microwell arrays that allow imaging each cell then retrieving it for sequencing, giving direct phenotype-genotype linkage
Perturbing the stability of the primed state (chromatin modifiers, DOT1L, KDM5) to test whether frequency of survivors can be tuned up or down
Testing whether surviving colonies are transcriptionally equivalent to each other or form distinct resistant fate classes
Whole-genome sequencing of survivor clones to firmly exclude cryptic genetic variants and copy-number differences
Measuring transcriptional burst kinetics of resistance genes to ask whether priming reflects burst frequency versus burst size
Degron or inducible expression of candidate priming genes at tunable levels to map a dose-response between state and survival probability
Timing experiments varying drug exposure onset to test whether priming windows are periodic or random in time
